extracted.intended_audience: EPA staff and program/regional personnel developing regulatory actions
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for EPA staff to identify, evaluate, and address environmental justice (EJ) considerations during the development of regulatory actions, and to determine when actions raise EJ concerns and require public engagement. The document is intended to foster consistent EJ consideration across EPA programs and regions and to protect historically underrepresented communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask questions and evaluate environmental justice considerations at key points in the rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidance is a step-by-step guide that helps EPA staff ask questions and evaluate environmental justice considerations at key points in the rulemaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the step-by-step questions in the Guidance to systematically identify EJ issues during scoping, analysis, drafting, and review stages of a regulatory action; follow the sequence provided to ensure EJ considerations are not overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether actions raise possible environmental justice concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: It helps EPA staff determine whether actions raise possible environmental justice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether proposed regulatory actions would have disproportionate adverse effects on minority, low-income, indigenous populations, or tribes; document findings and, where concerns exist, consider mitigation, alternatives, or additional outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and facilitate public participation in the rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidance encourages public participation in the rulemaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and implement outreach and engagement strategies to solicit input from affected and historically underrepresented communities; ensure opportunities for meaningful participation are provided early and throughout the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency with EPA programs and regional EJ efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Created to ensure understanding and foster consistency with efforts across EPA’s programs and regions to consider environmental justice and make a visible difference in America’s communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align analytic approaches, decision points, and outreach practices with other EPA program and regional guidance to promote consistent EJ consideration across the Agency; coordinate with program/regional EJ leads as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on protecting historically underrepresented and at-risk populations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide is part of EPA’s efforts to advance environmental justice and to protect the health and safety of the historically underrepresented in the environmental decision-making process—minority, low-income, and indigenous populations, and tribes—who are often most at risk from environmental hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating impacts and designing mitigation or engagement, prioritize identification of exposures, vulnerabilities, and barriers to participation affecting minority, low‑income, indigenous populations, and tribes; tailor analyses and outreach to those community contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the final Guidance (supersedes the July 2010 Interim Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has issued final Guidance on Considering Environmental Justice During the Development of a Regulatory Action. The final guidance supersedes the agency’s Interim Guidance on Considering Environmental Justice During the Development of an Action, released in July 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the final 56‑page Guidance and accompanying cover memo as the authoritative reference for EJ considerations in regulatory development; note the availability of PDF files and that a PDF reader may be required.
